{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABZiP2VA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhDJD38", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 53, "title": "Complete hit-test subscriptions, ray bindings and virtual-room AR placement", "body": "## Problem

At dev `0080e7a7aaa769becb9f9484ac98df77a6b6ec93`, hit-test subscriptions validate but discard `entityTypes`; transient profiles bypass DOMString conversion; `XRRay` skips dictionary conversion and retains detached matrices; transient result arrays are mutable. Request/frame operations also lack complete interface-brand and conversion-before-state checks. Applications can receive incorrect matches, reject legal inputs or corrupt retained results.

## Expected outcome

Provide coherent persistent and transient virtual-room hit testing, including converted subscriptions, useful plane/mesh filtering, correct ray/result bindings and predictable lifetime. Demonstrate visible placement through unchanged pinned AR applications.

Keep `hit-test` enabled for Quest MR and Android AR `immersive-ar`. Preserve required-feature rejection and optional omission for Quest VR and inline; this mode restriction is emulator policy. Virtual geometry is legitimate simulated environmental data. Feature-point generation and other unfinished modules remain future compatibility work.

## Context

Implementation spans `src/polyfill/api/XRRay.ts`, both source/result pairs, `runtime.ts`, shared brands, `EmulatedXRDevice.ts` and `ARScene.ts`. `environment.ts` and `plane-regions.ts` already describe the same room through mesh triangles and plane regions. Extend these dependencies together where necessary; UI work is unnecessary unless needed to exercise the API.

Use [Hit Test WD 2025-12-11](https://www.w3.org/TR/2025/WD-webxr-hit-test-1-20251211/), [Device CRD 2026-06-09](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-webxr-20260609/) and [WebIDL 622910c](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/622910c67c724e362f71e8255a0380bade261acb/index.bs). Preserve these revisions.

Retain this requirement correction in the Issue/PR: the existing AI-authored implementation assumes empty entity lists and any list containing `point` require `NotSupportedError`. The pinned Hit Test §§3–7 instead retain supplied lists and filter candidates. Therefore accept these legal subscriptions: an empty list produces no hits; absent point data produces no point hits without suppressing requested plane/mesh results. This conclusion follows the pinned algorithms, rather than an explicit unsupported-type exception. Also distinguish unrestricted-double origin members from restricted-double direction members when correcting ray conversion.

All 52 inspected Issues/PRs are closed. Earlier #11/#19 work was partial; #51/#52 addressed planes rather than this subscription scope. Existing R51 reports integrated nominal hits, and R37 reports historical Firefox placement. Neither establishes these missing contracts or current Chromium Three.js hit-test placement. Inspected WPT code is not passing execution evidence.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Convert request arguments before feature/lifecycle checks: required dictionaries/members, inherited members in IDL order, one-shot iterable snapshots, enum coercion, DOMString profiles and genuine space/ray interfaces. Invalid bindings reject request Promises with `TypeError`. After conversion, absent `hit-test` rejects with `NotSupportedError`; an enabled ended session rejects with `InvalidStateError`. Conversion failures leave no subscription behind.
- [ ] Correct both `XRRay` overloads, numeric conversion/defaults, zero-direction and homogeneous-coordinate `TypeError` checks, normalization and transform-derived rays. Preserve readonly origin/direction identity and cached matrix identity until detachment; regenerate transferred matrices. Exported matrix writes must not change subscription geometry. Cover translated, rotated and opposite-direction rays using pinned WPT assertions and [Chromium’s detached-matrix implementation](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/f842f52ef39fd97b449eb27cff414bf05a98ddce/third_party/blink/renderer/modules/xr/xr_ray.cc).
- [ ] Retain effective entity selections and apply genuine candidate classification. Default to planes; distinguish plane, mesh, mixed, empty and point-without-data requests. Prove filtering with independently classified virtual fixtures, while allowing coincident plane/mesh room surfaces. Verify offsets, reference-space offsets, viewer movement, misses, nearest-first persistent results and surface-normal-aligned poses. Do not impose an otherwise unspecified orientation around the normal.
- [ ] Make source/result interfaces nonconstructible and their public operations/accessors branded, with appropriate descriptors and readonly data. Accept genuine objects across separately injected same-origin realms; reject forged/proxied receivers and arguments. Transient groups retain their input source and frozen results; returned sequence containers cannot mutate frame maps.
- [ ] Exercise persistent sources and Android’s matching `generic-touchscreen` transient input across press, movement, release and reacquisition; unmatched profiles yield no groups. Preserve per-frame snapshots: cancellation does not erase an already computed current-frame entry, but later frames lack it. Repeated cancellation throws `InvalidStateError`; missing/foreign frame-map entries and inactive result access also throw `InvalidStateError` after binding conversion. Foreign pose base spaces reject, unavailable poses return null, and shutdown releases backend subscriptions without contaminating restarted sessions. Preserve existing foreign subscription-space rejection as explicit emulator policy; do not attribute an absent request-step check to the draft. Preserve affected hit-result anchor integration.
- [ ] Run unchanged [Samples `hit-test.html` at fb41c34](https://github.com/immersive-web/webxr-samples/blob/fb41c3416496974672e2c766a41c6febcba2d07e/hit-test.html) and [Three.js r186 `webxr_ar_hittest.html` at 9b4a2ac](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/9b4a2ac29c63ccb43fd51c5661f2f873ac2c39b8/examples/webxr_ar_hittest.html) on both AR profiles in Chromium and Firefox: eight combinations. Use the actual extension and genuine panel routes. Record moving reticles, independently checked placement positions, visible placed objects, Quest stereo/Android mono pixels, end/restart and cleanup. Preserve application requests and capability exposure; observers must retain calls, results and exceptions.
- [ ] Coordinator runs `npm run build:firefox`, focused hit-test contracts through the existing Chromium/Firefox driver infrastructure, and `npm run test:environment` for affected shared geometry. Add documented focused selectors where needed; current `test:wpt` does not select hit-test cases. Adapt pinned WPT setup explicitly, including differences in post-end cancellation and orientation assumptions. Run affected regressions selected from the actual changes, without a generic verification rerun or additional AI re-review.
- [ ] Update the inventory and reproduction record with exact commands/selectors, tested revision, browser/tool versions, served application/dependency hashes, observations, failures, skips and instrumentation. Keep historical failures distinct from final results. Record any further mistaken AI requirement with its original assumption, correction, primary evidence and rationale, without human approval or independent AI re-review; preserve meaningful acceptance.

## Optional validation

Additional offset-space combinations or independently authored irregular rooms, when they add coverage beyond mandatory cases.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WebXR API compatibility goal for
Quest 3 VR/MR and Android AR. Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance
criteria when primary specifications or measured evidence establish the correction.
Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
